newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower as origin selling continued to outweigh industry buying. November ended $14 lower at $1,618 per tonne. In New York arabica futures ended unchanged to slightly higher in quiet trade, boosted by light fund buying. September closed 80 points higher at 128.10 cents/lb while December added 50 points to close at 117.05 cents/lb. Traders said the recent price slide has encouraged some roaster buying although funds are still long, which could weigh on prices. Broker Merrill Lynch said that a 50 per cent retracement of the recent rally, that was mostly fund inspired, leaves room for coffee to break as low as 112.50 cents/lb basis December and that there is a good chance that this will develop.

BRAZIL - Coffee exporters have been delaying coffee shipments while a bill removing a 13 per cent export tax, the so-called ICMS tax, makes its way through congress. The bill, aimed at boosting competitiveness of Brazilian commodities abroad, is slated to go for a Senate vote in the second week of September.
After a Senate approval the bill must be sanctioned by president Fernando Henrique Cardoso, and will take effect only after being published in the country's Official Gazette.

Exporters are delaying coffee shipments because they want to increase profits by not paying any export tax. Some even speculate that the export tax exemption could affect world market prices because Brazilian coffee would be cheaper compared with the coffee from other countries. However, it is too early to say, what effect the measure will have.

NICARAGUA - Nicaragua's coffee production is threatened by the government's failure to repair roads and bridges damaged by hurricane Cesar, the president of Nicaragua's Coffee Growers Union (UNICAFE) said. He added 460,000 60-kg bags of coffee are in danger of being lost.
UNICAFE projected Nicaragua's 1996/97 coffee production at 822,000 bags, down from 921,000 bags produced in 1995/96.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 269,529 bags of coffee in May 1996, 49 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.278 million bags, 17 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 18 per cent to 2.783 million bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Costa Rica (121,700 vs 167,600 bags), Colombia (115,400 vs 85,700 bags) and Vietnam (147,800 vs 63,200 bags). The country exported 239,900 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 8.5 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 20 per cent to 538,400 bags.
